models.title: Current-price gross value added from industry output
models.summary: Industry contribution to GDP from gross output less intermediate inputs. The residual includes labor compensation, net production taxes and gross operating surplus, rather than representing firm profit.

relationship.original_equation: Value added = gross output - intermediate inputs.
relationship.locator: Glossary opening definition and equivalent income components
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced GO,II,VA label the source prose quantities. Currency-currency=currency on a common current-price interval basis. Gross means before consumption of fixed capital; do not replace GO with final sales or II with total expenses. Same price/boundary conventions are essential; no claim that incompatible tax valuations cancel automatically. Nonnegative ordinary GO and II are an explicit application profile, not a restriction on the signed residual VA. Output may be negative if intermediate consumption exceeds output. Named value-added definition is distinct from b06 economic profit, which subtracts explicit and opportunity costs.

variables.definition: Gross value of industry production for both final and intermediate uses during the period.
variables.context: Same industry/sector, domestic production boundary, accounting interval, source vintage, current-price USD scale and compatible industry-account valuation conventions. GO is gross production, including intermediate sales; II is corresponding intermediate consumption, not labor compensation or fixed-asset acquisitions. This is a period flow, not capital wealth.

variables.definition: Current value of goods and purchased services consumed as intermediate production inputs under the source accounts.
variables.context: Same industry/sector, domestic production boundary, accounting interval, source vintage, current-price USD scale and compatible industry-account valuation conventions. GO is gross production, including intermediate sales; II is corresponding intermediate consumption, not labor compensation or fixed-asset acquisitions. This is a period flow, not capital wealth.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative ordinary intermediate-consumption profile; excludes compensation and capital formation.

variables.definition: Signed industry contribution to domestic product before economic depreciation, using matching industry-account valuation.
variables.context: Same industry/sector, domestic production boundary, accounting interval, source vintage, current-price USD scale and compatible industry-account valuation conventions. GO is gross production, including intermediate sales; II is corresponding intermediate consumption, not labor compensation or fixed-asset acquisitions. This is a period flow, not capital wealth.
variables.domain: Finite signed; may be zero or negative, with no invented profitability restriction.

assumptions: Source definition: use gross output and intermediate consumption for the same industry-account boundary and period.
Application profile: nonnegative ordinary output and intermediate-consumption amounts, retaining the signed difference.
limitations: Not revenue less all expenses, economic profit, net value added or a stock valuation.
Inputs require compatible accounts/tax valuations; no model for computing intermediate consumption or deflating components is supplied.

models.inverse_notes: GO=VA+II and II=GO-VA are unique with the other two known; no denominator or roots. Require recovered GO,II>=0, while VA remains signed. Check VA600,II400 recovers GO1000 and forward600; GO500,VA-100 recovers II600 and forward-100. At VA0, GO=II>=0, and either known amount determines the other. VA alone leaves both inputs underdetermined, including the zero case. Inversion does not determine account classification.

gaps: New industry gross-output, intermediate-consumption and gross-value-added meanings. Currency-only binding to profit or final expenditure would be semantically invalid.

models.title: Fixed-capital stock balance in common reference prices
models.summary: One-period Laspeyres-volume capital-stock reconciliation including investment, economic depreciation and other disappearance. It is an accounting balance with supplied components, not a depreciation calibration or a forecast.

relationship.translation_notes: Local K0 maps S^K(t-1), K1 maps S^K(t), I maps I^K(t), D maps D^K(t), O maps O^K(t). CAD_ref denotes reference-price monetary representation of volume, with the same reference period for every term; source K is a volume superscript, not a price index or physical unit. Dimensions reference_currency+reference_currency-reference_currency-reference_currency=reference_currency. Integrated investment/consumption/disappearance amounts can be added to stock changes, while rates require integration first. I remains signed for net acquisitions less disposals; a declaration of net versus gross acquisition convention must match this account. Application profile treats D and O as nonnegative removals and requires a nonnegative closing stock; unrepresented other appearances/reclassifications must be absent or accounted separately before using this restricted four-component balance. No revaluation term occurs because all terms share fixed reference prices; current-price and historical-cost stock updates are outside scope.

variables.definition: Opening net fixed-capital stock volume in the selected fixed reference-price valuation.
variables.context: Same fixed-capital asset population, ownership/sector/geographic boundary, contiguous period (t-1,t], and one common fixed reference-price Laspeyres valuation in CAD_ref. K0,K1 are endpoint stock volumes expressed at reference prices. I,D,O are integrated period amounts on that same basis, not instantaneous rates, annualized flows or current-price CFC. Economic depreciation D includes normal deterioration/obsolescence/ordinary accidental damage; O is separately classified other disappearance, avoiding double counting.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; same surviving asset population and scope as closing stock.

variables.definition: Integrated investment volume over the interval in the source-compatible acquisitions/disposals convention.
variables.context: Same fixed-capital asset population, ownership/sector/geographic boundary, contiguous period (t-1,t], and one common fixed reference-price Laspeyres valuation in CAD_ref. K0,K1 are endpoint stock volumes expressed at reference prices. I,D,O are integrated period amounts on that same basis, not instantaneous rates, annualized flows or current-price CFC. Economic depreciation D includes normal deterioration/obsolescence/ordinary accidental damage; O is separately classified other disappearance, avoiding double counting.
variables.domain: Finite signed; negative net acquisitions allowed only with a consistent asset balance and nonnegative K1.

variables.definition: Integrated economic depreciation volume for normal deterioration, obsolescence and ordinary accidental damage.
variables.context: Same fixed-capital asset population, ownership/sector/geographic boundary, contiguous period (t-1,t], and one common fixed reference-price Laspeyres valuation in CAD_ref. K0,K1 are endpoint stock volumes expressed at reference prices. I,D,O are integrated period amounts on that same basis, not instantaneous rates, annualized flows or current-price CFC. Economic depreciation D includes normal deterioration/obsolescence/ordinary accidental damage; O is separately classified other disappearance, avoiding double counting.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative removal; not tax/book depreciation or current-price CFC.

variables.definition: Integrated other disappearance volume, such as exceptional catastrophe loss, excluded from D.
variables.context: Same fixed-capital asset population, ownership/sector/geographic boundary, contiguous period (t-1,t], and one common fixed reference-price Laspeyres valuation in CAD_ref. K0,K1 are endpoint stock volumes expressed at reference prices. I,D,O are integrated period amounts on that same basis, not instantaneous rates, annualized flows or current-price CFC. Economic depreciation D includes normal deterioration/obsolescence/ordinary accidental damage; O is separately classified other disappearance, avoiding double counting.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative removal in this profile; positive appearances and sector reclassifications need separate accounting.

variables.definition: Closing net fixed-capital stock volume on the same reference-price basis and asset/ownership boundary.
variables.context: Same fixed-capital asset population, ownership/sector/geographic boundary, contiguous period (t-1,t], and one common fixed reference-price Laspeyres valuation in CAD_ref. K0,K1 are endpoint stock volumes expressed at reference prices. I,D,O are integrated period amounts on that same basis, not instantaneous rates, annualized flows or current-price CFC. Economic depreciation D includes normal deterioration/obsolescence/ordinary accidental damage; O is separately classified other disappearance, avoiding double counting.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative under account-consistency guard; a negative stock signals incompatible flow inputs.

assumptions: Source equation: all components are Laspeyres volume measures; stock endpoints bracket the exact period over which flows accumulate.
Source classification: consumption of fixed capital is economic depreciation, while other disappearance includes separately classified exceptional loss.
Application profile: nonnegative stock and removals, with no omitted positive appearances or reclassifications; signed investment follows matching acquisition/disposal convention.
limitations: Does not estimate D, choose an asset life/depreciation function, predict investment or infer catastrophe losses.
Cannot apply directly to mixed historical prices, nominal/current-price balances or independently chained nonadditive measures; revaluation and omitted volume changes need separate accounts.

Closing inventory63+7+25=95, independently assembled by surviving cohorts rather than reordering aggregate balance.

references.method: Independent surviving-asset inventory: opening asset A30 sold intact and removed from this ownership boundary; asset B70 suffers normal decline5 and closes65. No other assets remain. Signed investment-30 reflects the disposal; closing65 independently counted.
Admitted accounting boundary: the sole opening asset is fully economically consumed by the end of the interval, with no replacement or exceptional loss; closing asset stock is zero.

Other disappearance missing; cannot silently assume absent catastrophic or other removals.

models.inverse_notes: Unique additive inverses with the other four quantities known: K0=K1-I+D+O; I=K1-K0+D+O; D=K0+I-O-K1; O=K0+I-D-K1. No division or root; retain K0,K1,D,O>=0, signed I and compatible account classifications. Cohort case K195,K0100,D10,O20 gives I25; forward95. Net-disposal case K165,K0100,D5,O0 gives I-30; forward65. At K1=0 the balance K0+I=D+O is nonsingular for a single unknown, but without separate D/O measurements it cannot allocate ordinary versus exceptional loss. Zero opening stock is allowed when current-period investment supplies nonnegative closing stock/removals.

gaps: New fixed-reference CAD volume and capital-account meanings. b03 current-price consumption_of_fixed_capital cannot bind to D without a separately supported valuation conversion; endpoint stock quantity repeats with different time context.
Source's Eq7.19 depreciation function f and average-life calibration are not executable inputs here; they are deferred, not filled with guessed constants.

models.title: Quantity-weighted mean price of an identical product
models.summary: Average observed transaction unit value defined by total transaction value over corresponding total quantity. Prices may differ between transactions, while the product and additive quantity unit remain identical.

relationship.original_equation: P_bar = V_bar/Q_bar = sum_i p_i q_i / sum_i q_i.
relationship.translation_notes: Local pbar,V,Q map source barred P,V,Q. Vector sums are not evaluated by this scalar model: V and Q must be independently aggregated over the same transaction set. Dimensions CAD/U=currency U^-1. Source supports the weighted-mean interpretation only for identical products; adding heterogeneous quantities would destroy it. Application profile nonnegative transaction quantities and prices admits free transactions, excludes net-return/negative-weight aggregates. This named mean price is not a new solve direction of a constant-price revenue equation: individual transaction prices can differ and output is the quantity-weighted aggregate.

variables.definition: Total actual value of the identical-product transactions in the declared interval and valuation basis.
variables.context: Same set of actual transactions in one identical, quality-consistent product/service, common additive physical unit and CAD transaction valuation/boundary, across the declared observation interval. V aggregates transaction values and Q aggregates matching purchased/sold quantities; each transaction quantity is nonnegative and Q>0. This is a quantity-weighted transaction mean, not average production cost, a quoted fixed price, or an index spanning different products.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative in nonnegative-price transaction profile.

variables.definition: Total additive quantity of the identical product across exactly the transactions counted in V.
variables.context: Same set of actual transactions in one identical, quality-consistent product/service, common additive physical unit and CAD transaction valuation/boundary, across the declared observation interval. V aggregates transaction values and Q aggregates matching purchased/sold quantities; each transaction quantity is nonnegative and Q>0. This is a quantity-weighted transaction mean, not average production cost, a quoted fixed price, or an index spanning different products.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive, with nonnegative component transaction quantities.

variables.definition: Observed transaction-price mean weighted by corresponding transacted quantities.
variables.context: Same set of actual transactions in one identical, quality-consistent product/service, common additive physical unit and CAD transaction valuation/boundary, across the declared observation interval. V aggregates transaction values and Q aggregates matching purchased/sold quantities; each transaction quantity is nonnegative and Q>0. This is a quantity-weighted transaction mean, not average production cost, a quoted fixed price, or an index spanning different products.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero if all positive-quantity transactions are free.

assumptions: Source restriction: all transactions pertain to an identical product with an additive common quantity unit.
Application profile: nonnegative quantities and prices, same currency/transaction valuation, no net-return or negative-weight aggregation.
limitations: Not an aggregate price level for heterogeneous goods, average unit production cost or a forecast selling price.
Changes in transaction composition can change this average; a comparison over time requires identical quality and appropriately matched scope, and is not automatically a pure-price index.

models.inverse_notes: V=pbar*Q for pbar>=0,Q>0, unique. Q=V/pbar requires pbar>0,V>0 to recover a positive quantity; retain the identical transaction-set context. Check pbar2.5,Q4 recovers V10; V10,pbar2.5 recovers Q4, forward2.5. At pbar=V=0 any Q>0 fits; pbar0,V>0 is inconsistent. If V0,pbar>0, inversion gives excluded Q0. Inversion does not recover the distribution of individual transaction prices or a causal price/quantity relation.

gaps: New CAD and mean-transaction-price meanings, with transaction quantity distinct from produced quantity. Same dimensions as unit cost do not justify binding those meanings.
